items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Earl Phillips was on drums, and Jimmy Boyle was playing piano. And we were working at a place called the Flame

ctx.x: So I began playing the drums in the church. By then, the church had broke up -- this had to be around 1930 -- the church was small and the congregation was small; everybody was very poor. I think they lost the big church they had with the Crash, because they had to take smaller living quarters, and like I said, I was staying with Mr. and Mrs. Turner at that time.

And I was playing. In church, we had a piano player, Mrs. Phillips, and Billy Johnson played great cymbals. We didn't have no horns, or at least I didn't see no horns over at their house -- just people clapping their hands, and
tambourines and singing. But it was a beautiful feeling -- a beautiful feeling. And that started me off.
